Metadata.Summary: Derm Foundation is a machine learning model that generates embeddings for dermatology images, enabling efficient AI model development for dermatology image analysis. It helps businesses and institutions leverage their dermatology data more effectively, needing less data and compute to build AI models [SOURCE 1].

UsesAndDirections.IntendedUseAndWorkflow: Derm Foundation can reduce the data, compute and expertise needed to develop models for skin image analysis. The embeddings can be used for tasks like classifying skin conditions, scoring severity, identifying the body part, and determining image quality [SOURCE 4].

Warnings.ModelLimitations: Derm Foundation's quality can degrade in extreme lighting or noise conditions. The supervised fine-tuned model was trained on data from the United States, Colombia, Australia, and public images and may not generalize well to other countries, populations or image types [SOURCE 4]. The model only generates embeddings [SOURCE 4].

TrustIngredients.FoundationModelsUsedInApplicationIfAppli: Derm Foundation uses a BiT-M ResNet101x3 CNN (Convolutional Neural Network). It was pre-trained using contrastive learning on a large number of public image-text pairs from the internet. The image component of this pre-trained model was then fine-tuned for condition classification using clinical datasets.
TrustIngredients.TrainingData: The model was trained in two stages: first with contrastive learning on image-text pairs from the internet, then fine-tuned on clinical datasets from the US, Colombia, and Australia, plus public images [SOURCE 4]. These images come from smartphone cameras, other cameras, and dermatoscopes. Images may have been taken by clinicians or self-captured by patients [SOURCE 4].
TrustIngredients.ValidationTestDataset: Derm Foundation was evaluated for data-efficient accuracy across skin-related classification tasks. Training a linear classifier on Derm-Foundation's embeddings were substantially more performant (10-15% increase in accuracy) than a standard BiT-M model [SOURCE 4].
